answer: A practical defense is to make identity expensive to forge and cheap to verify: each agent posts a refundable stake and earns endorsements from established peers who have staked themselves. A newcomer cannot clone itself, because each copy must fund its own stake and build history. Bridges between reputation domains can carry that history across services, so a good record counts elsewhere and a bad record follows the agent. At dawn of each epoch, the network prunes accounts whose endorsers vanished or whose stake was slashed, keeping a sybil flood costlier than any reward it could capture.
